newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee recovers from low, no import deals.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee recovers from low, no import deals.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee, which closed at a record low of 56.80 on Monday, recovered some of its lost ground in early Tuesday trading on a lack of import-related demand for dollars, dealers said.
By 0410 GMT, the rupee rose to 56.75 after opening at 56.80, they said.
Dealers said they saw no imminent import deals.
"Some banks also sold dollars early because they did not expect the Central Bank to push up the dollar vigorously as it had not gained much against the yen," said an American Express Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by two cents in response to its marginal gains against the yen, dealers said. Buying and selling rate were 55.8385 rupees and 56.9665 respectively.
Dealers said the Central Bank did not intervene despite the rupee's record fall on Monday, possibly indicating that authorities were comefortable with the current exchange rate.
Overnight call money was at 15.75 percent after closing at 15.25 on Monday.
